root_cause.text: The Arm Ethos-U GEM command-stream parser in `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate()` increments the output index for a 64-bit command word without revalidating the `size/4` bound, allowing an unchecked write past the end of the DMA-backed `bocmds` buffer when the last command has bit 14 set.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (i >= size / 4) return -EINVAL;` immediately after `i++;` and before `bocmds[i] = cmds[1];`, matching the described bug where the loop already used `bocmds[i] = cmds[0]` and then performed a second, unchecked write after incrementing `i`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check to prevent out-of-range command buffer writes during commandstream validation.
intent_record.what: In the commandstream copy-and-validate loop, after incrementing the command index `i`, the code now checks `if (i >= size / 4)` and returns `-EINVAL` before writing `bocmds[i] = cmds[1];`.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from writing past the end of the `bocmds` buffer when the incremented index would exceed the number of 32-bit words available, turning a potential out-of-bounds access into an explicit invalid-argument failure.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check to prevent out-of-range command buffer writes during commandstream validation.

relevance_review.reason: The group’s intent matches the root cause: it adds a bounds check in commandstream validation to prevent an out-of-range write when processing Ethos-U GEM commands, which directly addresses the unchecked buffer write described.

candidates.rationale: This increments the output index for the second 64-bit command word without any accompanying revalidation of the buffer bound, which is the direct step that can lead to writing past the end of the DMA-backed bocmds buffer.
This is the unchecked write to the command buffer that becomes out-of-bounds when i was incremented past size/4 due to the missing bounds check for the last command with bit 14 set.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable parser logic is present in `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate()`. The loop is `for (i = 0; i < size / 4; i++)`, but inside it, a 64-bit command consumes an extra word when `cmd & 0x4000` is set: `if (get_user(cmds[1], ucmds++)) ...; i++; bocmds[i] = cmds[1];`. There is no recheck of the `size / 4` bound after incrementing `i`, so a final 64-bit command can advance `i` past the end of the DMA-backed `bocmds` buffer and write out of bounds. The fix is not present here because there is no additional bound validation before `bocmds[i] = cmds[1]` and no adjustment of the loop condition to account for the second word.
